title: Distributed Inner-Product Estimation for Continuous-Variable Quantum States
authors: Jun Tang, Congcong Zheng, Xutao Yu, Zaichen Zhang
abstract: Distributed inner product estimation (DIPE) is a fundamental task in quantum information, aiming to estimate the inner product between two unknown quantum states prepared on distributed quantum platforms. For multimode continuous-variable (CV) systems, the infinite-dimensional Hilbert space poses an additional challenge. In this work, we develop a CV-DIPE protocol using only local homodyne measurements at shared phase settings and classical communication. Under a known bound on the mean energy per mode, we derive explicit finite-sample guarantees and sufficient copy counts for estimating the full inner product to prescribed accuracy and confidence. The energy constraint yields an inverse-square truncation-bias bound, while Gaussian structure strengthens the tail control to exponential decay and improves the resulting accuracy scaling. Numerical simulations with Gaussian and non-Gaussian states illustrate the balance between truncation bias and statistical error and its dependence on mode number and energy. Our results enable independent CV platforms to benchmark their state preparations against one another, even when neither state admits a tractable classical description.
summary: This paper develops a protocol to estimate the inner product between two unknown continuous-variable quantum states prepared on separate, distributed platforms using only local homodyne measurements. By analyzing the required measurement resources, the authors provide explicit sample complexity bounds, showing how the required data scales differently for general versus Gaussian states, which is vital for experimental quantum networking.
main_problem: The paper addresses Distributed Inner-Product Estimation (DIPE) for continuous-variable (CV) quantum states, which is crucial for benchmarking state preparations across independent quantum platforms.
main_result: They derive finite-sample guarantees for estimating the inner product using only local homodyne measurements and classical communication, providing distinct scaling laws for general and Gaussian states.
method: The estimation relies on approximating the infinite-dimensional inner product integral via truncation in phase space, followed by constructing an unbiased estimator based on multiple independent homodyne measurement settings.
model_or_system: The system involves multimode bosonic CV quantum states, whose properties are analyzed using their characteristic functions and covariance matrices, measured via local homodyne detection.
